items.look_for: 192 tiles of 16x32, shown 16 per row in index order (entry i at column i%16, row i/16). White = terrain in front (hides the sprite), transparent = sprite shows. Shapes should read as bottom-anchored terrain silhouettes (tree trunks/canopies, wall and building edges), not noise. masks.json states the bit layout: 64 bytes per entry, one big-endian 16-bit word per row, MSB = leftmost pixel. This is the game's complete mask store (shadow_mem, 192 x 64 B). The terra data references entries 0-170: 160 are applied with a non-zero occlusion mode; 11 have pixels but are never referenced ([18, 44, 84, 85, 93, 94, 147, 148, 154, 159, 160]); 171-191 are blank filler. Look at a spread of the referenced ones: tree canopies, wall tops, building edges, bridge rails; none should be noise.
items.title: Terrain occlusion masks — 192 entries 16x32, 1 bit/pixel (ADF blocks 896-919)

T2.3.summary: One 1-bit PNG per terrain occlusion mask (192 x 16x32) decoded from ADF blocks 896-919 (shadow_mem), a contact sheet of all entries, and masks.json describing the bit layout and how the game indexes entries (byte 0 of a tile's terra_mem record -> maskit -> entry * 64 bytes).
